title: try, catch, finally, and filters
hook: try marks risky work. catch handles a type you understand. finally always runs for that try. when filters let you catch a subset without eating the rest.

sections.heading: Control flow
sections.prose: When an exception is thrown, the runtime finds the first catch whose type is compatible, after evaluating when if present. More derived types must be listed first or the compiler errors. finally runs whether the try succeeded, caught, or rethrew — it is the primitive using is built on (last topic). A return inside try still runs finally before the method actually returns. catch without a type (bare catch) exists for non-CLS exceptions; you almost never need it in application code.

sections.heading: when filters
sections.prose: catch (HttpRequestException ex) when (ex.StatusCode == HttpStatusCode.TooManyRequests) handles throttling and lets other HTTP failures bubble. The filter should be fast and side-effect free; throwing inside a filter is a nasty edge. Filters keep SQS workers from wrapping every exception in the same retry policy. Cancellation: catch (OperationCanceledException) when (ct.IsCancellationRequested) is the usual pattern so you do not hide unexpected cancellations.

snippets.label: Ordered catch plus a when filter
snippets.explanation: Cancellation rethrows. 429 retries. Other HTTP failures log and throw;. Lease release always runs.

sections.heading: What not to catch
sections.prose: catch (Exception) at a low helper is how bugs go silent. Catch at a boundary where you can restore state (module 06 hierarchy topic). Logging inside a filter is clever and wrong. Do not use finally to swallow — if finally throws, it can hide the original exception.

interviewTakeaways: Most-derived catch first; finally always runs for that try.
when filters select without catching sibling failures.
catch (Exception) belongs at process or message boundaries, if at all, and should rethrow when lost.

jsTsCorrelations.note: JS has the same three keywords but no typed catch (except optional catch binding). There is no when filter.
TS cannot catch only TypeError at the type level. C# can catch only IOException.
